content_sections.body_text: Use was/were + verb-ing for the action already in progress: ‘I was running home when the rain started.’ Here run means move on foot faster than walking. Draw a long line for was running and a point where the rain started.
content_sections.title: Retrieve scene and movement

content_sections.body_text: Mai: ‘I was running home when the rain started. Please help me carry these books.’ An: ‘Yes. Put them in my bag.’ Mai: ‘Thank you.’ The opening explains the situation, the request names the need, and the reply supplies relevant help.
content_sections.title: Connect request and response

content_sections.body_text: Retell in order: ‘First, Mai was running home. Then rain started. Next, she requested help. Finally, An carried the BOOKS.’ Make BOOKS more prominent when correcting ‘the bag’; make AN prominent when correcting ‘Mai.’ Focus follows the new contrast.
content_sections.title: Sequence and focus the account

content_sections.body_text: Create a new four-event account: ongoing movement, interruption, help request, relevant response. Rehearse each group before joining them. Record the final account. Check that run keeps its foot-movement sense, event order is clear, the response solves the stated need, and only the intended new word is most prominent.
